# Healthcare Pulse

> Independent weekly analysis of India's healthcare and digital health systems, written by Mayank Madhur, Practice Leader for Healthcare and Life Sciences at HFS Research. Every edition is original analysis built on primary government data (NFHS, MoHFW Health Dynamics of India, National Health Accounts, NITI Aayog), published every Friday since April 2025.

Healthcare Pulse publishes two kinds of content: weekly long-form editions that make a single argument from primary data, and free interactive data trackers that let anyone explore the underlying state-level numbers themselves.

All data trackers are original work. They are built by transcribing and verifying figures directly from government source publications, with printed page numbers cited. They are not aggregated from third-party datasets.

Author: Mayank Madhur, Chennai, India. Contact: mayank@mayankmadhur.in
Site: https://mayankmadhur.in

## Interactive data tools (original datasets)

- [India C-Section Tracker](https://mayankmadhur.in/tools/csection/): Caesarean section rates for all 33 Indian states and union territories from NFHS-6, with the private-versus-public split and the trend since NFHS-5. Telangana is highest at 62.2%.
- [Rural Health Capacity Tracker](https://mayankmadhur.in/tools/rural-pyramid/): Specialist vacancy, generalist doctor and nursing shortfalls across 35 Indian states, from MoHFW Health Dynamics of India 2023-24. 63% of specialist posts at rural Community Health Centres are vacant; Madhya Pradesh has filled 71 of 1,308 sanctioned posts.
- [Fertility Transition Tracker](https://mayankmadhur.in/tools/fertility/): Total fertility rate by state from NFHS-6, showing India below replacement at 2.0 and 1.6 in urban areas, with the four-times spread across states.
- [Autism in India Data Dashboard](https://mayankmadhur.in/tools/autism/): Prevalence by measurement method, the diagnosis-age gap, state early-intervention capacity, financing and workforce, with full sources.
- [India Digital Health Adoption Index](https://mayankmadhur.in/tools/health-stack/): Adoption of India's digital health stack.
- [Which of the Four Indias Are You In?](https://mayankmadhur.in/tools/which-india/): Six questions that place a household in one of India's four health financing tiers.
- [The Value Chain, Tier by Tier](https://mayankmadhur.in/tools/health-value-chain/): Where the patient, the money and the medical record break across six steps of care, for each of the four financing tiers.
- [Healthcare Financing Atlas](https://mayankmadhur.in/tools/health-financing/): How 180 countries finance health, classified with the official SHA 2011 financing schemes rather than Beveridge and Bismarck labels. 95 of the 180 are mixed or segmented. Europe is 3% mixed; Africa is 81%. Every row carries an evidence grade, and live out-of-pocket, government and external spending shares load from the WHO GHED mirror.
- [The Value Lens](https://mayankmadhur.in/tools/value-lens/): Nine health economics lenses applied to the same two options at once, so they can be seen to disagree. Cost-effectiveness, cost-utility, cost-benefit, cost-minimisation, budget impact, ROI, cost of illness, cost-consequence and efficiency, each with its formula, when to use it, where it breaks and how it gets misused.
- [All tools](https://mayankmadhur.in/index-tool/): Full index of interactive trackers.

## Recent editions

- [Edition 74: Stop Asking What Healthcare Costs. Ask What It Buys.](https://mayankmadhur.in/edition-74-healthcare-cost-effectiveness.html): Price tells you what one unit costs, not what it achieves. Nine ways of asking whether a health intervention is worth it, and why they give different answers to the same question.
- [Edition 73: Adding Beds Is the Easy Part](https://mayankmadhur.in/edition-73-hospital-capital.html): Indian hospital groups grew revenue 21% and beds 15% while margins stayed near 23%. A new bed loses money before it makes any. The claim that filling beds widens margins does not survive testing.
- [Edition 72: India Doesn't Have a Financing Model](https://mayankmadhur.in/edition-72-india-financing-180.html): 95 of 180 countries are mixed or segmented. Europe is the only region where the textbook models dominate, which is where they were written.
- [Edition 71: India Reaches Almost Every Pregnant Woman Once](https://mayankmadhur.in/edition-71-mother-baby-journey.html): 95.9% see a health worker once, 65.2% complete four visits, 15.3% of toddlers eat an adequate diet. India solved arrival and still measures arrival.
- [Edition 70: You Cannot Fix an Org Chart With an API](https://mayankmadhur.in/edition-70-swasth-bharat.html): The Swasth Bharat Portal is the right architecture. Convergence is real at the interface and absent underneath, because budgets and reporting lines did not move.
- [Edition 68: Four Indias, One Shared Bill](https://mayankmadhur.in/edition-68-one-fix-four-indias.html): India runs four health systems under one name, each breaking at a different point in the same six-step chain. Medicines are the shared exposure.
- [Edition 54: The Four Indias of Healthcare](https://mayankmadhur.in/edition-54-four-indias.html): Why "pan-India" is usually a lie. Four markets with different economics and failure modes.

## Key site sections

- [Research](https://mayankmadhur.in/research/): Original long-form research, including the THRIVE-SDOH strategic framework.

- [Ask](https://mayankmadhur.in/ask/): Question-answering across the full archive.

## Topics covered

Policy, Strategy, Digital Health, Governance, Pharma, Biotech, Geopolitics, applied to Indian healthcare. Recurring subjects include Ayushman Bharat and PM-JAY, ABDM and ABHA, the DPDP Act, health financing and out-of-pocket spending, the rural health workforce, NFHS survey data, medical devices, telemedicine and eSanjeevani, and health insurance design.

Content may be quoted with attribution to Healthcare Pulse by Mayank Madhur and a link to the source page on https://mayankmadhur.in. Data figures are transcribed from cited government publications; the source and page number are stated in each edition's footer.
